messages.message: ### Step 2: Direct Translation Translate each source line into German, guided by the Reference Translation and Step 1 analysis. Output: ONE German line per source line (preserve line count and end punctuation). Rules: - Follow the meaning from Reference Translation. - For "so X that Y": keep resultative structure, do NOT convert to "because". - No internal punctuation; copy only end punctuation from source.
so mein Geist, der noch flog, wandte sich zurück um den Pass erneut zu betrachten der nie eine lebende Person verließ.

### Step 3: Word Table & Coverage Check Build a word table from Step 2 translation, mapping each source word to its target equivalent. Output: ONE Markdown table (all lines combined). Columns: [Source Word] | [Contextual Definition] | [Target Word/Phrase] | [Back-Translation] | [Status: OK/MISSING/WRONG/GRAMMAR/UNNECESSARY] Mark GRAMMAR for agreement errors (gender, number, case) or other grammatical mistakes. Mark UNNECESSARY for elements present in source but not needed in target language (e.g., articles that target language omits naturally). After the table, list any MISSING, WRONG, GRAMMAR, or UNNECESSARY items.

| Source Word | Contextual Definition | Target Word / Phrase | Back‑Translation | Status | |-------------|----------------------|----------------------|------------------|--------| | così | resultative adverb linking the previous clause | **so** | “so” | OK | | l'animo | noun, the speaker’s soul | **Geist** | “spirit / soul” | OK | | mio | possessive adjective | **mein** | “my” | OK | | ch'ancor | relative pronoun + adverb “still” | **der noch** | “who/which still” | OK | | fuggiva | imperfect verb “was fleeing” | **flog** | “flew” | OK | | si | reflexive clitic | **sich** | “himself” | OK | | volse | past verb “turned” | **wandte** | “turned” | OK | | a *(first)* | preposition indicating direction “to” (part of *a retro*) | **zurück** | “back” | OK | | retro | noun used adverbially “back” (already expressed by *zurück*) | — | — | **UNNECESSARY** | | a *(second)* | preposition introducing purpose infinitive | **um** | “to / for” | OK | | rimirar | infinitive “to look again” | **betrachten** | “to look at / consider” | OK | | lo | definite article, masculine accusative | **den** | “the” (acc.) | OK | | passo | noun “pass” | **Pass** | “pass” | OK | | che | relative pronoun | **der** | “which” | OK | | non | negation particle | **nie** | “never” | OK | | lasciò | past verb “left” | **verließ** | “left” | OK | | già | adverb “already” (temporal intensifier) | — | — | **MISSING** | | mai | adverb “never” (intensifier) | — | — | **UNNECESSARY** | | persona | noun “person” | **Person** | “person” | OK | | viva | adjective “living” | **lebende** | “living” | OK | | — | — | **eine** (added article before *lebende Person*) | “a” | **UNNECESSARY** |
### Items to Address - **MISSING:** *già* – the temporal intensifier “already” is not rendered in the German version. - **UNNECESSARY:** *retro* (its meaning is covered by *zurück*), *mai* (redundant because *nie* already expresses the negation), and the inserted article **eine** (German requires an article here, but the source Italian does not have one).
No grammatical mismatches were detected; all agreements (gender, number, case) are correct.

### Step 4: Correction & Final Output Fix any MISSING, WRONG, or GRAMMAR items from Step 3. Reorder within line if needed; do not add new content words.
